page: Amazon Web Services r3.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance utilizing the Xen hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 8 dedicated vCPUs derived from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 61.0 GB of system memory, yielding 7.62 GB of RAM per core, and includes 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. The baseline network bandwidth is rated at 1 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across multi-core and memory operations, contrasted by weaker single-core capabilities. The stress-ng single-core CPU performance is categorized in the bottom 25%, while multi-core performance falls in the middle 50%. Memory bandwidth tests show average throughput, with read-only small block cached speeds reaching 386.23 GB/sec and large block uncached writes at 40.68 GB/sec. Geekbench scores reflect a poor single-core rating of 726.0 and a weak multi-core rating of 2768.0, though software compilation with Clang and image processing achieve average tier results.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and average database operation benchmarks, this instance is designed for memory-intensive workloads that do not require high single-threaded CPU performance. It is appropriate for database operations, caching layers, and memory-bound processing tasks. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile offers a high density of memory relative to compute resources, though the older Intel Xeon architecture presents a tradeoff in raw processing speed compared to newer generations.
description: Amazon Web Services r3.2xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2670 v2 processor running at 2.5 GHz on the Xen hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated vCPUs across 4 physical cores, 61.0 GB of RAM, and 160 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. While single-core CPU benchmarks, such as Geekbench and stress-ng, place the instance in the lower performance tiers, its multi-core capabilities and memory bandwidth consistently register in the average range. Specifically, memory read-only small block cached bandwidth reaches 386.23 GB/sec. Lacking a GPU and featuring a baseline network bandwidth of 1 Gbps, this instance is optimized for memory-dense workloads. It is best suited for database operations, caching systems, and memory-bound applications where high memory capacity is prioritized over high-speed single-threaded compute performance.
